HMW-V14: FM Job Timeline — Time as Hero Data

Vendor Design Hypotheses · Teleport OS

"How might we render the FM pickup and delivery times as the primary visual anchor in the job timeline section, so dispatchers can immediately assess urgency without parsing a cluttered datetime string?"
Context: FM Trucking jobs have a defined pickup datetime (origin.date) and delivery datetime (destination.date). These are the most operationally critical data points for the dispatcher — they determine whether the driver needs to leave immediately or has lead time. The design spec says "Times are the most important data for FM." Currently, renderRoute() calls fmtDateMono() which strips the time component and shows only dd MMM at 9px as a sub-line below the location name. There is no time shown at all. This is a gap between spec and implementation.

Dispatcher's first question: "When does my driver need to be at pickup?" — not "where is the pickup?" They already know the facilities; urgency drives dispatch, not geography.

Option A — Current (Baseline)

Location names are primary (11px bold). Date shown as 9px sub-line in #374151. Time component stripped by fmtDateMono() — only dd MMM visible. Dispatcher cannot assess urgency without mentally parsing "25 Aug" into a time of day. Section titled "Route" (not "Timeline").
❌ Not compliant with spec

Cons

· Section titled "Route" — misleading for pickup/delivery context

Option B — Time as Hero (Spec-aligned)

Pickup and delivery times rendered at 20px JetBrains Mono — the single largest text element on the page after the job service name. Date shown at 10px below the time. Location name at 10px below the date, muted. Two-column layout with arrow divider. Section retitled "Pickup / Delivery" to match the two-point nature.

Dispatcher sees the critical info in one glance: "09:00 → 14:00". The rest is context.

Pros

· Directly matches spec ("pickup datetime in big mono")

· Location name preserved as secondary context

Cons
· Larger vertical footprint than Option A
· If no time is set (only date), shows midnight "00:00" unless handled
· Long location names truncate — fix with ellipsis on .time-loc

Option C — Two-Row Split (Times Row + Locations Row)

Times occupy a dedicated tinted row at the top (18px JetBrains Mono, ghost background). Location names occupy a second row below. Structural separation signals the information hierarchy without requiring the dispatcher to parse vertical proximity. Useful when location names are long and would crowd the time display.
⚠ More complex for marginal gain

Cons

· Option B already achieves hierarchy without needing structural separation

✓ Decision: Option B — Time as Hero

Adopt Option B. The dispatcher's core question is when, not where. Showing the pickup time at 20px JetBrains Mono as the first visible data point in the section answers that question in <1 second. Location name is secondary context — preserved at 10px below the date. The section should be retitled "Pickup / Delivery" to accurately reflect its two-point nature.

Option C is rejected: the two-row separation adds visual complexity without meaningful gain over B. Option A is rejected: showing only "25 Aug" at 9px actively hides urgency.

Implementation notes:

  • Use fmtTime(origin.date) for the hero time (HH:MM, 20px mono). Fall back to "—" if no date set.
  • Use fmtDateShort(origin.date) for the secondary date line (dd MMM yyyy, 10px mono, #6b7280).
  • Location name: 10px, #6b7280, overflow ellipsis. Not the hero — don't make it bold.
  • Rename section from "Route" to "Pickup / Delivery" in renderRoute() (or rename the function to renderTimeline()).
  • If origin.date is null: show "—" at 20px mono for the time slot and "No date set" at 10px for the date line.
  • No tinted row (Option C), no background change — the design system does not use tinted rows in the section body.

Open question: When the pickup time is within 2 hours from now, should the time hero color change to #dc2626 (urgency red) as a scalar signal? The admin app uses red urgency coloring in the Pickup Date column. This would close the urgency loop for dispatchers. Recommend: yes, align with admin pattern — same threshold (2h), same color. Needs user input to confirm.
